prerequisites: Competencies taught in the basic modules Linear Algebra I and Analysis I or Fundamentals of Linear Algebra and Fundamentals of Analysis are recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Students know the structural foundations of linear optimization problems and understand the basic mode of operation of these methods.
Students can present the meaning of central concepts, for example from duality theory, and recognize them in the discussion of optimization problems.
Students know the structural foundations of integer optimization problems and understand the basic mode of operation of these methods.
Students know methods of Operations Research.
Students have the basic knowledge for advanced modules on general optimization problems.
Students are able to apply mathematical working methods (developing mathematical intuition and its formal justification, training abstract thinking, proving).
Students are able to speak freely about scientific content, both in front of an audience and in a discussion.

assessment_methods.method: Oral examination (individual examination) or written exam

assessment_rules: Grading is done with 0 to 15 points according to the examination regulations for the B.Sc. Business Informatics degree program. To acquire credit points, at least 50 percent of the points from the weekly exercises must be achieved. The examination performance is either an oral examination or a written exam.
bibliography: Matthias Gerdts Frank Lempio, Mathematische Optimierungsverfahren des Operations Research, De Gruyter, 2010
